1fc7vld: Dear Paula: thank you for the proposal to organize a series of talks in our space. The topic coincides with one of our lines of work, and we particularly value that it includes meetings open to the neighborhood. After reviewing the calendar, I am afraid we cannot take on the full series on the dates proposed. During that period we share the room with another association and we do not have the equipment needed to broadcast all the sessions. We prefer to explain these limits before reserving dates that we might not be able to sustain.
w3uau6: We could, however, consider an in-person session in November, provided it is limited to fifty attendees and the organizers take charge of registration. This possibility is not yet a confirmation: we would need to know the budget and check staff availability. Would you mind sending us an adjusted version before the fifteenth? If that format does not meet your goals, we will understand if you look for another venue. We would not want our partial proposal to delay decisions that you need to make now.
9a21eb: Regarding publicity, it would be advisable to distinguish collaboration on one activity from institutional endorsement of the whole program. We can include the confirmed meeting in our calendar, but not authorize the use of the logo in materials for sessions we do not organize. Perhaps this is not the most convenient solution for the campaign, although we believe it will avoid confusion about responsibilities and resources. If we do go ahead, we will agree in writing on the presentation text and the conditions for using the image.
1gkvhem: I appreciate that you thought of us and I hope this reply allows you to weigh a realistic alternative. We will keep the November possibility open until we receive your proposal, without reserving the room yet. I remain at your disposal to clarify the conditions set out. Sincerely, Marina, center coordination. The courtesy of the message does not remove the rejection of the full series; it helps to express it in a way that lets the other party decide with enough information.
